game.intro: December walked in carrying a clipboard. Saturn is thrilled. Everyone else, please answer from the heart.
game.question: Pick one December job you would happily do every single day of the month.

game.intro: Someone gave the label maker a mind of its own. Our camera wants in on the chaos. Lens to the face, please.
game.prompt: Any word printed on something in your home: a jar, a box, a button. So close only a few letters show.

game.intro: Libra moon has the scales out and they wobble. Saturn says fairness is overrated tonight. Be magnificently wrong.
game.question: What does a set of balance scales actually measure?

game.intro: Matching scarves in two towns, same colour, same hour. DES. The sound booth is wrapped in wool and ready.
game.prompt: Getting bundled up to go outside in December: zipper, boots, a sigh, the door. Make it all with your mouth.

game.intro: Scorpio moon found the secret drawer and it is rifling through it. Confess nothing. Spell everything in tiny pictures.
game.prompt: Something people hide in a drawer and forget about for years. Emoji only.

game.intro: The moon is at five percent and fading. Tonight two of your stories are true and one goes into the lost-and-found.
game.prompt: Three things you found this year that you weren't looking for. One never happened.

game.intro: New moon, arrow away! Sagittarius is cheering from the rafters. Three pairs, ten seconds, aim and fire.
Zero percent moon. The studio lights are off except one lamp. Whisper your answers. Saturn whispers back.
game.question: On the darkest kind of evening, which glow would you most want nearby?

game.intro: Snowball dare day. The camera dares you to get uncomfortably close to something cold. Brave lens, brave you.
game.prompt: Something frozen, frosty or icy. Window frost, a freezer shelf, a snowbank. Fill the whole frame.

game.intro: The moon came home to Capricorn and Saturn is weeping into his gavel. Celebrate him by getting this very wrong.
game.question: What is a mountain, really?

game.intro: The kettle is slow tonight and the whole studio is waiting. Fill the silence for it. Kindly. Eventually.
game.prompt: A kettle that is taking far too long, from the first tick to the triumphant boil.

game.intro: Twelve twelve on the twelfth of the twelfth. Don't even scream. The newsroom clocks have unionized.
game.headline: CLOCKS ACROSS ATLANTIC CANADA STOP AT 12:12 TO ___

game.intro: Umbrellas are flipped, mischief is up, and Saturn has a tarot question. Fitting, since you two own the deck.
game.question: How many cards make up the Major Arcana in a standard tarot deck?
game.source: Standard 78-card tarot: 22 Major Arcana (The Fool 0 to The World XXI) + 56 Minor Arcana

game.intro: Mars and Saturn lined up and borrowed the thunder. The buzzer is rumbling. Three pairs. Go loud.
Pisces moon, fishbowl vibes. Nothing tonight has to make sense, including this question. Especially this question.
game.question: In tonight's dream you can breathe underwater. Where do you swim first?

game.intro: The oars got lighter today. The camera wants to see what's lighter in your world. Extreme close-up, featherweight edition.
game.prompt: Something lighter than a slice of bread: a feather, a tea bag, a receipt, a leaf. Get closer than polite.

game.intro: The moon is visiting the Tiger, so tonight the answers should roar. Wrongly. With full chest. Saturn has earplugs.
game.question: How do tigers get their stripes?

game.intro: A mitten ran away and left a trail. Tonight we hear the escape. Contestants, cue the chase music.
game.prompt: A mitten making a daring escape: sliding off a radiator, down the stairs, out the door, into a snowbank.

game.intro: Pencils sharpened, nagging jobs finished. Reward yourselves with crayons, but tiny digital ones.
game.prompt: A chore you finally finished this month, told as an epic quest. Emoji only.

game.intro: Fourth cookie day. Taurus moon is relaxed and very full of crumbs. Tell three tales, but only two with sprinkles of truth.
game.prompt: Three holiday traditions from when you were small. One is made up.

game.intro: Eve of the longest night. The lights dim one notch per answer. Hurry, contestants, before we're all in the dark.
HAPPY BIRTHDAY, NANCY! Solstice, full moon, and the light comes back. Don't even scream. Saturn is crying.
game.question: The light is returning tonight. Where should the first new sunbeam land?

game.intro: The real Full Moon Recharge! Stones under the moon, cameras in hand. Show us the sparkle. Way up close.
game.prompt: Something that shines or sparkles: a stone, tinsel, a spoon, a frosted window. Close enough to lose its shape.

game.intro: Lit windows tonight, all across two towns. Inside the studio, though, the facts have gone home early.
game.question: Why do people put lights in their windows in December?

game.intro: Happy Christmas from the studio! The crew is in paper crowns. Saturn is on his second helping. Make some merry noise.
game.prompt: One sound from your Christmas Day: wrapping paper, a cracker, a dog with a new toy, a crowded table.

game.intro: Lion nap day. The whole newsroom is asleep under its desks, so you two write the front page. Quietly.
game.headline: LOCAL LION REFUSES TO LEAVE NAP SPOT, CITES ___

game.intro: Leo wants a grand entrance, so here's a grand number. It sits between two birthdays. Do not go over.
game.question: How many days is it from Nancy's birthday (Dec 22, 2026) to Joel's next birthday (Mar 21, 2027)?
game.source: Date arithmetic: Dec 22 to Dec 31 = 9, January 31, February 28 (2027 not a leap year), March 21 = 89

game.intro: The wishing well is empty and the year is nearly swept up. Three quick picks. Keep the good ones.
Identical mugs, two kitchens, one shopping trip nobody took. DES, year-end edition. Saturn needs a lie down.
game.question: Which kind of coincidence delights you the most?

game.intro: The boat touched shore. The crossing is done. The camera wants one last mysterious close-up before the year docks.
game.prompt: Something that reminds you of this whole year. Zoom in so far the other has to guess from one detail.

game.intro: New Year's Eve! The Fire meets the Mountain at midnight. Until then, every answer must be gorgeously wrong.
game.question: Why does the new year start at midnight and not at breakfast?
